hypotheses.claim: Weakest regimes on dev_24 are capacity_level=tight (vbs_rel_gap -22.16%), depot_style=eccentric (-19.67%), and size=100 (-20.44%). Under tight capacity, single-client removal savings are dominated by the packing structure, not by geometric detour: removing a light customer from a near-full route frees usable load slack that enables profitable reinsertion, whereas removing a heavy customer from a slack route rarely opens new configurations. Therefore a multiplicative ruin score of the form score_i = rank_power(|removal_savings_i|/scale * gate_rdist * gate_load * gate_depot, p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio)) with gate_load = (route_load/C + demand_i/C)^beta strongly favoring high-utilization routes, and exponent p rising from ~0.5 (near-uniform, exploratory) at early iter_frac to ≥1.5 late/stagnating, will lower the mean objective on the tight-capacity and eccentric-depot subsets relative to the round-1 champion (mean 16.0818, 215 ms mean, 24/24 wins) without exceeding the 500 ms deadline, since the O(n) scoring pass is negligible versus the deterministic Regret-2 reinsertion inner loop.

next_search_advice.direction: Tight-capacity-aware multiplicative ruin scoring: amplify load-utilization saturation and route-distance gates inside score_ruin_nodes, with iter_frac-driven rank-power sharpening that is shallow early (diversify) and steep late (intensify)
